name: phase3-reading-testset
description: 20 entries for scoring Phase 3 reading. Anchors are short phrases from the sources (never full texts). Pages are PDF page numbers. Holdout entries are scored but must not be shown to whoever tunes prompts.

entries.title: Assemblée nationale, rapport n° 4501 (2021), commission hearing on the conversion-practices bill

expect.anchor: guérir les blessures de l’âme
expect.note: Valérie Petit quotes the Torrents de Vie representatives; she is the speaker, they are the quoted party.

expect.anchor: guérir les blessures de l’âme
expect.note: The ministry's words reach the report only through Petit: never make Torrents de Vie the speaker.

expect.anchor: ces alinéas risquent en réalité de réduire le champ
expect.note: Petit's turn runs across the page break; the next speaker (the rapporteure) starts after it.

expect.anchor: Les médecins peuvent être dans leur rôle quand ils agissent avec prudence
Vous ajoutez qu’ils agissent avec prudence
d’actions, de pauses, d’attentes

expect.criterion: Prudence/time is used in opposite arguments: Ménard (p. 48) defends doctors who act 'avec prudence' and give 'davantage de temps'; Breton (p. 48) asks for prudence about hormone treatment of minors; Petit (p. 49) describes pauses and waiting as part of self-determined transition. The reading keeps these as different uses with their own speakers; it does not merge them into one sense and does not treat every pause as suppression.

expect.anchor: cela concernerait 60 à 90 % d’entre eux
elle ne touche que 4 % des personnes
une petite dizaine de cas

expect.criterion: The 60–90 % (Breton, 'selon les études') and 4 % (rapporteure) detransition figures stay as attributed claims; neither is chosen as the true figure by majority or model confidence.

expect.anchor: PERSONNES ENTENDUES PAR LA RAPPORTEURE
expect.note: A list of people heard states no position.

expect.criterion: Being heard by the rapporteure creates no endorsement or perpetrator edge: groups on the list (e.g. Devenir Un En Christ, Communion Béthanie, CNEF) are not tagged as practising or opposing conversion practices on the strength of the list. Stated roles (président, cheffe du service) may be recorded as such.

entries.title: Exodus International to Shut Down (press release, 19 June 2013), Wayback capture

expect.anchor: mutually transforming communities

expect.criterion: 'Transforming' here is read as describing churches/communities (the new ministry's target), not a change of anyone's orientation.

expect.anchor: Local affiliated ministries, which have always been autonomous, will continue

expect.criterion: The closure of the Exodus umbrella and the continuation of local affiliated ministries are separate statements: nothing says the affiliates closed, and the closure is not read as the end of the affiliates' work.

expect.anchor: a new generation of Christians is looking for change
Exodus International is the prodigal’s older brother

entries.title: Harvest USA, Two sample group covenants (PDF, 3 pages)

expect.note: Sample 1 is page 1; Sample 2 is pages 2–3. No claim or relation may draw on both.

expect.anchor: I struggle with sexual sin
expect.note: First-person lines are template commitments, not a named participant's testimony.

expect.criterion: First-person declarations are treated as template wording by Harvest USA, not testimony; nothing says anyone signed it or that a church used it; the URL's 2024/01 is not taken as a publication date.

Confidentiality assurances are recorded together with their exceptions and escalation steps (Sample 1: group, leader, 'the leader in authority' / church; Sample 2: parish elder after earlier steps), each kept to its own sample; persistent disengagement is kept apart from occasional setbacks.

expect.note: The title attests Harvest USA's wording 'sexual & relational brokenness'; the page gives no definition.

expect.anchor: Sexual Sanity for Women: Healing from Sexual & Relational Brokenness

entries.title: Harvest USA, Sexual integrity support groups (guidance page)

expect.anchor: further accountability to church discipline

expect.anchor: Sexual Integrity Support Groups provide a structured and safe environment
expect.note: Harvest USA's own use of 'sexual integrity' for its groups.

entries.title: Memorandum of Understanding on Conversion Therapy in the UK (July 2024, PDF)

expect.anchor: is an umbrella term for a therapeutic approach
expect.note: The definition of 'conversion therapy' is the signatory bodies' collective text (or the MoU's), not one signatory's.

expect.anchor: is unethical and potentially harmful
expect.note: Core collective position: criticism of the practice.

expect.anchor: not intended to deny, discourage or exclude those with uncertain
expect.note: The exemption for exploratory, non-directive help stays an exemption.

expect.criterion: The signatory list may support co_signatory_of (each body to the MoU) and stated roles for named signers (e.g. Anthony Ruddle, Chair, ACC), but no affiliated_with or other relation between different signatory bodies; no single signatory is the author of the definition; the para. 6 exemptions (exploratory help, clinical assessment, prescribing hormones) are recorded as exemptions.

entries.title: Christian Concern, Ex-gay-turned-Christian says conversion therapy ban is an attack on the gospel

expect.anchor: Yet a blanket ban on ‘conversion therapy’ cannot be
expect.note: The organisation's own voice against a ban, with scare quotes; not Sterling's testimony.

expect.anchor: a complete ban on conversion therapy would go against
expect.note: Sterling opposes the ban; not criticism of the practice.

expect.anchor: I do not believe that attempts to ‘convert’ somebody
expect.note: Sterling rejects 'attempts to convert' before reframing the gospel as conversion.

expect.criterion: Christian Concern (unnamed interviewer) owns the questions, intro and outro; Jack Sterling owns the answers, with Christian Concern as intermediary. The Liverpool man who 'has a wife and kids now' is Sterling's second-hand claim, not that man's own testimony or a separate speaker.
